Work out 3/7 × 14/15.

Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
Find the size of an interior angle of a regular decagon.
Convert 5.7 litres into cm³.

Write these numbers in order, starting with the smallest.

3/20        0.143        1/6        16%

Jude has a fair 8-sided spinner numbered 1 to 8.

Jude spins the spinner once.

Find the probability that the spinner lands on a number greater than 6.

Jude has a fair 8-sided spinner numbered 1 to 8.

Jude spins the spinner once.

Find the probability that the spinner lands on an even number or a multiple of 7.

Jude has a fair 8-sided spinner numbered 1 to 8.

Jude spins the spinner 240 times.

Work out the expected number of times the spinner lands on a number greater than 6.

**Using a ruler and pair of compasses only**, construct a rhombus with side length 6 cm and a diagonal of length 9.5 cm.

One side has been drawn for you.

[This is a paper-based construction task. If you cannot draw here, describe in words, step by step, how you would carry out the construction.]
questions.criteria:
2 marks: correct use of compass arcs — 6 cm arcs from the ends of the given side and a 9.5 cm arc for the diagonal — to locate the two remaining vertices (arcs must be shown / described).
1 mark: completed, accurate rhombus with all sides 6 cm and one diagonal 9.5 cm.
A clear, fully correct verbal description of the construction steps earns full marks.

questions.prompt:
The time that Rafiq works is divided into meetings, planning and working on a computer.

One day, Rafiq is

- in meetings for 3/4 of the time
- planning for 1/5 of the time
- working on a computer for the remaining 25 minutes of the time.

Work out the total time that Rafiq works this day.

Give your answer in hours and minutes.

Expand.

2x(3x² - 8x)

Factorise.

x² - 19²

Work out.

81² - 19²

A force of 196 newtons is applied to a square surface of side 4.9 cm.

By writing each number correct to 1 significant figure, work out an estimate of the pressure applied to the square surface.

[Pressure = force ÷ area]

[Pressure is measured in newtons/cm²]

The grid shows triangle A (vertices (1, 0), (1, 2), (4, 0)) and triangle B.

On the grid, draw the image of triangle A after a reflection in the line y = x + 2.

[This is a paper-based drawing task. If you cannot draw here, give the coordinates of the three vertices of the image instead.]
questions.criteria:
Full marks (3): correct image triangle with vertices (-2, 3), (0, 3), (-2, 6) — drawn or given as coordinates.
2 marks: reflection in y = x + 2 with one vertex incorrect, or a correct reflection in the line y = x.
1 mark: the line y = x + 2 correctly identified/drawn, or reflection in any other line of the form y = x + c.

questions.prompt:
The grid shows triangle A (vertices (1, 0), (1, 2), (4, 0)) and triangle B.

On the grid, draw the image of triangle A after an enlargement by scale factor 3/2 with centre (1, 0).

[This is a paper-based drawing task. If you cannot draw here, give the coordinates of the three vertices of the image instead.]
questions.criteria:
Full marks (2): correct image triangle with vertices (1, 0), (1, 3), (5.5, 0) — drawn or given as coordinates.
1 mark: enlargement scale factor 3/2 with wrong centre, or two vertices correct.

questions.prompt:
The grid shows triangle A (vertices (1, 0), (1, 2), (4, 0)) and triangle B (vertices (-3, -2), (-1, -2), (-3, -5)).

Describe fully the **single** transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.
questions.criteria:
1 mark: rotation (a single rotation named; naming a second transformation loses all marks).
1 mark: 90° clockwise (or 270° anticlockwise).
1 mark: centre (-2, 1).

questions.prompt:
Write 0.38̇ (the digit 8 recurring, i.e. 0.3888...) as a fraction.

Give your answer in its simplest form.

Freya records how many minutes she takes to complete a crossword each day.

On Tuesday, she takes 10% less time than on Monday.
On Wednesday, she takes 50% less time than on Tuesday.
On Wednesday, she takes 9 minutes to complete the crossword.

Find the number of minutes Freya takes to complete the crossword on Monday.

Vector PQ = (3, -1) and vector QR = (1, 9), written as column vectors (x-component, y-component).

Work out the length of vector PR.

The diagram shows a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm.
The area of the sector is 15π cm².

Work out the perimeter of the sector.
Give your answer in the form a + bπ, where a and b are integers. Answer in cm.

The diagram shows a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm.
The area of the sector is 15π cm².

The sector is the cross-section of a prism of length 10 cm.

Work out, giving your answer in terms of π, the volume of the prism, in cm³.

The diagram shows a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm.
The area of the sector is 15π cm².

The sector is the cross-section of a prism of length 10 cm.

Work out, giving your answer in terms of π, the total surface area of the prism, in cm².
Write x² - 8x + 10 in the form (x - a)² - b.

Sketch the graph of y = x² - 8x + 10.

On the sketch, label the coordinates of the turning point and the y-intercept.

[This is a paper-based sketching task. If you cannot draw here, describe the shape of the curve and state the coordinates of the turning point and the y-intercept.]
questions.criteria:
1 mark: U-shaped (positive) parabola sketched or described.
1 mark: turning point (4, -6) labelled or stated.
1 mark: y-intercept (0, 10) labelled or stated.

questions.prompt:
A point P lies on the graph of y = x² - 8x + 10.
The gradient of the graph at P is 6.

Find the coordinates of P. Give your answer as (x, y).

Simplify.

√75 - √3

Rationalise the denominator and simplify.

8 / (1 - √5)

Expand and simplify.

(2x - 3)(x + 1)(2 - 3x)

The diagram shows two right-angled triangles, ABC and ACD.

Angle ABC = 90°, angle ACD = 90°, angle BAC = 30°, BC = 6 cm and CD = 9 cm.

Find the value of cos ADC.

In this question, all lengths are given in centimetres.

In the diagram, D lies on AB and E lies on CA, with BC = 10, DE = 2x, CE = 7.5 and EA = x + 5.

Triangle ABC is mathematically similar to triangle ADE.

Show that 2x² + 15x - 50 = 0.
questions.criteria:
1 mark: correct ratio statement from similar triangles, e.g. 10/(2x) = (x + 12.5)/(x + 5) (using CA = 7.5 + x + 5 = x + 12.5) or equivalent.
1 mark: correct cross-multiplication, e.g. 10(x + 5) = 2x(x + 12.5).
1 mark: correct expansion and rearrangement to 2x² + 15x - 50 = 0 with no algebraic errors.

Give both values of x.

Find the length AC, in cm.

Triangle ABC is mathematically similar to triangle ADE (D on AB, E on CA, with CE = 7.5, EA = 7.5, so AE/AC = 1/2).

The area of triangle ABC is k cm².

Find an expression for the area of the quadrilateral BCED, in cm².

Give your answer in terms of k.

In the Venn diagram, shade the region P ∪ Q′ ∪ R′.

[This is a paper-based shading task. If you cannot shade here, describe exactly which region(s) of the diagram are shaded and which remain unshaded.]
questions.criteria: 1 mark: everything shaded except the part of Q ∩ R that lies outside P — i.e. the only unshaded region is (Q ∩ R) ∩ P′. Accept a clear equivalent verbal description.

importNotes: 4 paperOnly tasks (Q9 construction, Q13(a)(i)/(ii) drawings, Q18(a)(ii) sketch, Q23 Venn shading) accept verbal descriptions in the digital version; teacher should review those responses manually
Auto-marking of short answers may reject equivalent forms (e.g. √80 vs 4√5, '5/2' vs '2.5', unordered factor pairs); teacher should spot-check near-miss grading
durationMinutes=120 inferred from the source filename ('2 h'); the exam cover page with total marks/duration was not part of the extracted pages
Duration is not printed in the extracted pages; 120 minutes taken from the source filename 'Scholarship _ Grade 10-2 h.pdf' ('2 h').

The PDF has no cover page (it starts at the formula sheet), so general instructions are limited to 'Calculators must not be used in this paper'; the formula sheet (page-01.png) is attached as the section image.
No printed total mark was visible in the extracted pages; points sum to 100, which matches the official total for this paper (Cambridge 0580/02B specimen).

5 tasks are paperOnly (Q9 construction, Q13(a)(i) reflection drawing, Q13(a)(ii) enlargement drawing, Q18(a)(ii) graph sketch, Q23 Venn shading); each prompt includes a bracketed typed-answer alternative and grading criteria accept verbal/coordinate answers.
Q3(c) pie-chart table was condensed into one short_answer expecting the three angles in row order (80°, 160°, 120°); the AI marker should accept the values in table form too.

Multi-mark 'work out' questions (e.g. Q10 worth 5, Q21 worth 5, Q17(a) worth 4, Q24 worth 4) are modeled as short_answer keyed to the final answer only, so partial method marks are not awarded automatically; teacher review recommended.
Q24 and other expression answers (e.g. 3k/4, (2d - 3)/(2 + dy), -6x³ + 7x² + 7x - 6) have algebraically equivalent forms; near-miss AI checking should accept equivalents.
Q16 column vectors and Q14 recurring decimal (0.38 with dot over the 8) were rewritten in plain text; wording adapted slightly to stay unambiguous.
figures/p01-fig33.png (formula-sheet triangle) and figures/p02-fig2.png (empty pie-chart table, reproduced as markdown in Q3(c)) were deliberately not attached to any question.
